name: Cryogen-free operation of a NIST 10 V programmable Josephson voltage standard at 4.3 K on a cryocooler with a supercritical-helium buffer
plain_name: Run the quantum volt standard on a cryocooler instead of liquid helium
description: The chip gave a 1.32 mA step width at 4.3 K with about 270 mW of net cooling, and kept quantum accuracy up to 4.8 K.
keywords: Run the quantum volt standard on a cryocooler instead of liquid helium

sources.citation: Rufenacht et al., Cryocooled 10 V Programmable Josephson Voltage Standard, IEEE TIM 64(6) (2015)
NIST publication record for the same paper

reported_equipment: cryocooler with a 3 kW water-cooled compressor

requirements.rationale: The step margins were measured at 4.3 K.
Quantum accuracy is lost above 4.8 K.
The procedure is defined as cryocooler operation.
The subarrays are current-biased and read out.

confirmation_note: Requirements taken from the cited procedure and independently re-verified against the source (research/v4, 2026-11-01). Users must confirm them for their own run; edits require confirmation again.
